description: Description Who is USP? The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. Brief Job Overview The Senior Scientific Community Engagement Specialist supports USP's global Advanced Manufacturing Technologies (AMT) and Resiliency Center initiatives by helping build and engage a scientific and technical community focused on pharmaceutical continuous manufacturing. This is an outward-facing community engagement role for someone who is comfortable working in a scientific or technical environment and enjoys connecting with people, building relationships, facilitating knowledge exchange, and identifying opportunities for meaningful engagement. The specialist manages the day-to-day operation of USP's online continuous manufacturing community at cmkc.usp.org while actively engaging scientific and technical stakeholders, supporting community programming and outreach, identifying relevant conversations and emerging needs, and connecting insights and people across the broader AMT network. The role does not require prior professional community management experience or expertise in continuous manufacturing, but it does require a working understanding of pharmaceutical manufacturing, curiosity about continuous and other advanced manufacturing technologies, strong communication and relationship-building skills, initiative, and an interest in learning and applying community engagement practices. This is not a laboratory or research role, and it is not an internal knowledge management role. It suits someone with a pharmaceutical manufacturing background who wants to work with people, such as through technical customer engagement, application support, scientific communications, or professional associations. The specialist works closely with the person leading USP's Continuous Manufacturing Knowledge Center (CMKC), adding dedicated capacity for ongoing community engagement, particularly with stakeholders in India, while contributing to broader programming, expert engagement, content, and knowledge-sharing activities. Training in community management and in using the online community platform will be provided. How will YOU create impact here at USP? As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. The Senior Scientific Community Engagement Specialist has the following responsibilities: Build relationships with scientific and technical stakeholders and conduct proactive outreach to encourage participation, identify interests and needs, and create opportunities for meaningful interaction across the AMT community. Support the development and growth of an India-focused AMT scientific community by identifying relevant stakeholders, developing connections, and linking India-based engagement with the broader global AMT community. Work with subject matter experts to identify valuable topics, questions, and resources, and connect people, ideas, and expertise across the community when opportunities for useful exchange or collaboration emerge. Scan the pharmaceutical manufacturing landscape for relevant journals, papers, conference talks, webinars, events, and regulatory updates; curate and share resources that address the community's interests and needs. Track community participation and engagement and recommend ways to improve the member experience and strengthen participation. Capture and organize knowledge from community activity, including recurring questions, expert answers, and emerging themes, so it can be easily found and reused by community members and across AMT programs. Other duties as assigned. Through this work, the PCM Scientific Community Engagement Specialist: Makes USP's online continuous manufacturing community an active, credible place where scientists, engineers, and regulators ask questions, share experience, and connect with experts. Grows USP's stakeholder network in India by building a regional scientific community that is connected to the broader global AMT community. Brings what is learned in the community, such as recurring questions, emerging needs, and expert contacts, back to AMT teams to inform programs, services, and future initiatives. Working knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing and the broader industry landscape (e.g., how medicines are developed, manufactured, and regulated), sufficient to follow technical discussions and communicate comfortably with technical experts and stakeholders. Expertise in continuous manufacturing is not required. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to understand technical information, ask thoughtful questions, and communicate effectively with subject matter experts. Demonstrated experience working with experts, customers, partners, professional stakeholders, or other external audiences. title: Senior Manager, Infrastructure Engineering
description: Senior Manager, Infrastructure Engineering We are seeking an experienced Infrastructure Engineer to design, operate, secure, and continuously improve enterprise infrastructure across on-premises and cloud environments. This position is entrusted with privileged Domain Administrator access for approved high-trust work and must apply disciplined change control, least-privilege practices, strong documentation, and sound engineering judgment. The engineer will serve as a senior technical resource for Microsoft identity and Windows platforms while contributing broadly to compute, virtualization, storage, backup, monitoring, automation, cloud, and disaster-recovery initiatives. The day-to-day responsibilities include but are not limited to: Privileged Domain and Identity Services Perform approved high-trust administrative work in enterprise Active Directory environments using designated, individually assigned privileged accounts. Administer and troubleshoot domain controllers, forests, domains, trusts, sites and services, replication, DNS, Group Policy, organizational units, service accounts, and authentication dependencies. Plan and execute sensitive directory changes, upgrades, migrations, consolidations, acquisitions, and recovery activities through formal change-management and peer-review processes. Protect privileged access through least privilege, separation of duties, multifactor authentication, secure administrative workstations, just-in-time or time-bound elevation where available, credential rotation, and auditable access reviews. Maintain the security and recoverability of identity services, including backup validation, authoritative and non-authoritative recovery procedures, break-glass controls, and tested runbooks. Investigate complex authentication, authorization, Kerberos, LDAP, DNS, replication, and Group Policy incidents; lead root-cause analysis and corrective actions. Partner with Cybersecurity, IAM, Audit, Compliance, Application, Network, and Cloud teams to remediate vulnerabilities and satisfy control requirements. Automate repeatable administration, reporting, health checks, and compliance evidence collection using PowerShell or comparable tools. Design, build, configure, patch, monitor, and support highly available Windows and Linux server platforms across data centers and public cloud environments. Engineer and support virtualization, compute, storage, backup, disaster recovery, monitoring, and core infrastructure services. Support hybrid-cloud workloads in Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services, including identity integration, networking dependencies, security controls, resilience, and cost-conscious design. Use infrastructure-as-code and configuration-management practices, such as Terraform, PowerShell, Ansible, Git, and CI/CD workflows, to deliver consistent and repeatable changes. Lead or contribute to infrastructure lifecycle projects, capacity planning, platform upgrades, migrations, technical debt reduction, and service improvements. Monitor performance, availability, security, capacity, and configuration compliance; address risks before they affect business services. Participate in incident, problem, change, release, and configuration-management processes and provide clear technical communications during major incidents. Create and maintain architecture diagrams, standards, operating procedures, build documents, recovery plans, and knowledge articles. Provide escalation support, mentor engineers, conduct technical reviews, and transfer knowledge across global teams. Participate in an on-call rotation and perform approved after-hours maintenance when required. Requirements: Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Five or more years of enterprise infrastructure engineering or systems administration experience, including substantial hands-on responsibility for Microsoft Active Directory. Demonstrated experience performing controlled work with Domain Administrator or comparably privileged credentials in large, complex, or regulated environments. Advanced knowledge of Active Directory Domain Services, Group Policy, DNS, Kerberos, LDAP, Windows Server, permissions, delegation, replication, and directory recovery. Strong understanding of privileged-access security, least privilege, role-based access, credential hygiene, logging, auditability, and separation of duties. Hands-on experience with PowerShell automation and source control. Working knowledge of virtualization, networking, storage, backup and recovery, monitoring, and cloud infrastructure. Experience with formal change management, incident response, root-cause analysis, and production support in a 24x7 environment. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaborate across technical and business teams. Ability to manage confidential information and privileged access with discretion, accountability, and sound judgment. Experience with multi-forest or multi-domain environments, mergers and acquisitions, domain migrations, or complex trust relationships. Experience with Microsoft Entra ID, hybrid identity, federation, single sign-on, multifactor authentication, PKI, managed service accounts, and privileged-access management platforms. Experience supporting VMware or comparable virtualization platforms; enterprise storage and backup technologies; and Azure or AWS services. Knowledge of security frameworks and controls such as Zero Trust, CIS benchmarks, NIST guidance, ISO 27001, or SOC 2. Relevant Microsoft, Azure, AWS, ITIL, or security certification.
